# Kammakkhandhaka (Kd 11)

**ID:** Kd 11  
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Kammakkhandhaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammakkhandhaka* is the opening chapter of the *Cullavagga* within the Khandhaka division of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; Williams 2005]. It provides detailed legal regulations governing the validity, enactment, offender duties, and eventual revocation of formal disciplinary procedures (*kamma*) initiated by the Saṅgha against offending monks [Vinayamukha 1983]. These disciplinary proceedings include censure or rebuke (*tajjanīyakamma*), subordination or guidance (*nissayakamma*), banishment from a locality (*pabbājanīyakamma*), reconciliation with laypersons (*paṭisāraṇīyakamma*), and suspension (*ukkhepanīyakamma*), the latter imposed for offences such as refusing to acknowledge or atone for an offence or refusing to renounce harmful views [Vinayamukha 1983; Sung 1999]. A monk undergoing such sanctions loses particular monastic privileges and may be prohibited from communal fellowship (*sambhoga*), requiring strict adherence to prescribed modes of conduct until formal restoration to full standing [Vinayamukha 1983; Banerjee 1979; Williams 2005].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd11 Pāṇḍulohitakavastu; xct-mu-kd11 Paṇḍulohitaka; lzh-mu-kd11 Paṇḍulohitaka; Lzh Sarv Kd11 Paṇḍulohitaka Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 11 Paṇḍulohitaka Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 10d d. Paṇḍulohitaka Khandhaka
- Passage-level parallels: AN 8.89 Paṭisāraṇīyasutta; MN 22 (PTS MN i 130) Alagaddūpama Sutta; Bu-Vb Pc68 Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 68; Bu-Vb Ss13 Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 13; Kd 15 Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn1 Vagga 1. Upasampadā; Pvr 7 Ekuttarikanaya
- Mentioned in: Cnd 23 Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa; Mnd 14 Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa; Pvr 17 Upālipañcaka

**Sources**

- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Documented the position of Kammakkhandhaka as the first chapter of the Cullavagga.
- [Williams 2005] Paul Williams (ed.), Buddhism: Critical Concepts in Religious Studies, Vol. 7 (2005) — Discussed the classification of the text as the section on legal acts and loss of privileges.
- [Vinayamukha 1983] Entrance to the Vinaya: Vinayamukha Vol. 3 (1983) — Described specific disciplinary procedures, including tajjanīyakamma and ukkhepanīyakamma, and prohibition of sambhoga.
- [Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-seng-chi'i-lu (Mahāsāṃghika) (1999) — Listed the five formal proceedings and correlated them with the Mahāsāṃghika Vinaya.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvastivada Literature (1979) — Noted correspondence between Kammakkhandhaka and the Tibetan Pāṇḍulohitakavastu regarding disciplinary measures and restoration.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Correlated Kammakkhandhaka with Pāṇḍulohitakavastu in comparative Vinaya literature.
